subject: N-mix study design question - truncate maximum possible count in field?

messages.author: 97512b0c9bacfbef
messages.subject: N-mix study design question - truncate maximum possible count in field?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working on revising an inherited protocol for monitoring amphibian breeding in vernal pools, specifically counts of egg masses.  Previously, "counts" have been binned into None (0), Low (1-10), Medium (11-50) or High (>50).  I'd like to move towards an N-mix modeling framework (using pcount and eventually pcountOpen) with repeated counts within a closed season.  Often pools have egg mass counts ranging from 0 to tens, but some pools may have many hundreds of egg masses, to the point where counting them becomes impractical given our staff capacity and limited time window for a closed season.  

My question is, what would be the statistical effect of stopping counts at a certain number, say, 50 or 100 egg masses, on N-mix model results and interpretation?  I have a mind to run some simulations as oft recommended by the gurus, simulating a population, sampling it, and then truncating counts >50 to 50 before running some models.  But, I'm having trouble thinking through the hypothetical ramifications of this type of data and how one would interpret estimated lambda.  I looked through old posts but haven't found anyone posting this type of situation - has anyone tackled this before?  

Thanks,
Alex

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] N-mix study design question - truncate maximum possible count in field?
parts:
Hi Alex,

you can't throw these data into the Nmix implementation of unmarked, because you have to formally acount for the binning of your data. This has been done before, see heer:

https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1890/13-2223.1

This binning modeling could be done in JAGS I think. Thorson usually works with ADMB or TMB, so surely this was done in that software.

Best regards ---- Marc
